subject: Follow-up: SLO/SLA details for Acme streaming use case
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Priya Malhotra <priya.malhotra@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 15:03:00 +0000
Subject: Follow-up: SLO/SLA details for Acme streaming use case

Hi Alex & Priya —

Great to meet earlier. Quick recap of what we discussed and proposed next steps so we can lock SLA language: 

- High-level workload: low-latency streaming generation for the Acme support assistant (token-by-token streaming to UI). Expected peak: ~600 qps, typical steady-state 250 qps. Concurrency target: bursts up to 1,000 concurrent requests for short windows.
- Latency targets (customer ask): P95 < 200 ms end-to-end for completed responses; P99 < 500 ms. For streaming we discussed initial-first-byte (time-to-first-token) target of < 100 ms and per-chunk (subsequent token batch) latency target of < 50 ms on our side.
- Throughput: sustainable throughput target 250 qps; ability to handle 600 qps burst for 10-15 min windows without queueing significantly.
- Measurement windows: discussed rolling 30-day windows for P95/P99 and weekly reporting cadence.
- Exclusions: responsibilities we identified include planned maintenance windows, customer-side networking issues, and spikes caused by malformed requests (we should define error classes).
- Remedies: we outlined standard service credit structure tied to availability SLOs; we need to align on both latency and availability remedies.

Attachments: I attached the draft SLO doc (SLO-draft-Acme-v1.pdf) and the network diagram you asked for (acme-network-diagram.png).

Next steps:
1) Vivek to confirm how Redwood measures latency (server-side vs end-to-end) and how streaming metrics are captured.
2) Acme to share a mock load profile (requests/sec over time) and example payload sizes.
3) We'll iterate on SLO language and schedule a 30-minute call to finalize SLA wording (proposed: Thu 16 Jul, 10:00 PT).

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0198
From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>

Cc: Priya Malhotra <priya.malhotra@acme.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: SLO/SLA details for Acme streaming use case

Thanks Marissa — helpful summary. A couple quick clarifications from our side before the call: 

1) Measurement scope: when you say P95/P99 latency, is that measured server-side (Redwood ingress -> response complete) or are you proposing an end-to-end measurement that includes our front-end and WAN? We have cross-team concerns about attributing network latency.

2) Streaming specifics: for the support assistant, the UX requirement is an initial-first-byte under 120ms from the moment the user hits send, then steady per-token latency so typing appears fluid. For long responses (~500-800 tokens) we care about overall completion time too (not just first token).

3) Concurrency and burst behavior: what’s the expected degradation profile when bursts exceed the reserved capacity? Do you have documented fallback behavior (queued requests, rate-limited, degrade to non-streaming responses)?

We'll share the mock load profile and sample payloads by EOD today. Also — please include any proposed SLA exclusion language you mentioned (maintenance windows, blackouts, force majeure) in the draft so we can review legally.

Alex
Product Lead, Search & Assist | Acme Corp
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acme.com>, Priya Malhotra <priya.malhotra@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 13:45:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Follow-up: SLO/SLA details for Acme streaming use case

Thanks Alex — quick technical answers below so you have something concrete before the call: 

- Latency measurement: Redwood reports server-side latency by default (ingress received -> final byte written). This is how we measure P95/P99 in the console and for SLO calculations.
  - End-to-end (E2E) measurement: we can support E2E reporting if you provide correlated client timestamps or app-side logs; we can ingest those or accept a signed sample. E2E would be separate and not primary for the SLA unless explicitly agreed.
- Streaming metrics: streaming is measured as two primary signals: time-to-first-token (TTFB) and per-chunk latency. TTFB is measured from ingress to first chunk write. Per-chunk latency is the mean within each request between chunk writes. For SLOs we typically surface TTFB P95/P99 and per-chunk P95 over the rolling window.
- Concurrency & burst behavior: with Dedicated capacity we can reserve headroom to hit your burst target. If bursts exceed reserved capacity we have policy options: autoscale (within limits), graceful degrade to lower-fidelity model, queueing with backpressure headers, or fallback to our regional Hosted endpoints. We can document the exact policy you'd like in the SLA.
- Exclusions: standard exclusions include planned maintenance (we provide >=48h notice and exclude the window), customer network outages, API misuse/spam or malformed payloads, and force majeure. We'll add example thresholds for what counts as "customer-side network" (e.g., >1% packet loss or >200ms RTT from major POPs).
- Reporting cadence & evidence: weekly SLO dashboards and monthly CSV exports; on-demand detailed buckets for root-cause analysis (RCAs) on incidents.
- Remedies: our standard is service credits tied to availability SLOs; for latency SLO misses we can define graduated credits or remediation commitments (e.g., 5% credit for each 0.1% availability delta below SLO up to a cap). We'll propose concrete numbers in the SLO draft.

I've attached the draft SLO doc (SLO-draft-Acme-v1.pdf) with the above items called out and a diagram (acme-network-diagram.png) showing where we'll collect server-side metrics. Please review and flag anything we should change before Thu.

— Vivek
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks again — this is great, Vivek.

Action items going into the Thu call:

- Redwood (Vivek): add explicit SLA text for latency measurement scope (server-side default + optional E2E), list of exclusions with examples and thresholds, and a proposed remedies table (credits + caps).
- Redwood (Marissa): schedule the final review call for SLA wording — proposed Thu 16 Jul 10:00 PT; I’ll send a calendar invite pending your confirmation.

If Thu doesn’t work, propose two alternate windows and we’ll accommodate. Looking forward to finishing this up — goal is to have signed language in our proposal next week so procurement can start redlines.

Best,
Marissa
